supplement_note: The list article indexes named biases, which is why it contains neither ego depletion nor power posing nor the bystander effect. Those are effects from the replication literature rather than entries in a taxonomy of biases, and they are the entries this site is best at. This supplement is that second source, assembled from the multi-laboratory projects rather than from any category listing. It now holds Many Labs 1 (16 effects, Table 2), Many Labs 2 (28 effects, Tables 2 and 5), Many Labs 3 (10 effects plus one conceptual replication and three added main effects, Table 3), Many Labs 4 (the single mortality-salience effect, read from the authors' preprint because the published Collabra PDF is behind a Cloudflare challenge), Many Labs 5 (10 findings, Tables 3 and 4), thirteen Registered Replication Reports from Perspectives on Psychological Science and AMPPS, and fourteen named effects from the Social Sciences Replication Project (Supplementary Tables 3 and 4). Three things are still missing. The Reproducibility Project: Psychology is present only as a project-level record, because its paper and supplement publish aggregate figures and leave the per-study effect sizes in an OSF data file. Several Registered Replication Reports carry a lab count and a direction but no effect size, because their abstracts give none and their full texts are paywalled; those rows say so in a numbers_not_obtained field. And the multi-lab replications that are not titled Registered Replication Reports, among them the disgust-and-moral-judgment and induced-compliance projects in AMPPS, have not been added at all.
